source_title: John Wood Group PLC Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report page 56 states that the directors' responsibility statement was approved by the Board on 5 March 2020; the exact Companies House filing bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue eased 1.2% to $9.89bn, while like-for-like adjusted EBITDA rose 5.4% to $704m and margin improved 40bps to 7.1%. Operating profit rose 83.6% to $303m, cash conversion reached 96% and net debt excluding leases fell 5.9% to $1.42bn, or 2.0x EBITDA. The order book declined 7.3% as legacy fixed-price work ran off and tender governance tightened. Management expected growth but identified early Covid-19 and oil-price uncertainty; completed disposals generated about $430m and reduced pro-forma leverage to 1.5x.
already_announced_exclusion: The nuclear and industrial-services disposals, portfolio optimisation, Technical Consulting Solutions combination, Amec Foster Wheeler integration and synergy programme, tender-governance changes and legacy fixed-price de-risking disclosed or completed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: A softer order book and emerging macro shock create limited pressure. Earnings and margins improved, cash conversion was strong, debt declined and completed disposals further strengthened leverage, providing very strong contrary evidence.

source_title: John Wood Group PLC Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 87, 88, 152 and 226 state that the strategic and directors' reports, responsibility statement and financial statements were approved by the Board on 19 April 2022; the exact Companies House filing bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Like-for-like revenue fell 14.2% and adjusted EBITDA fell 12.1% amid pandemic pressure and continued Projects weakness, although margin improved 40bps through mix, execution and cost efficiencies. The group recorded a $136m loss, including a $99m Aegis Poland charge and $78m restructuring costs. Free cash outflow was $398m, including a $306m working-capital outflow and $159m exceptional cash costs; net debt rose 37% to $1.39bn and leverage reached 3.3x against a 3.5x covenant. The order book rose 19% to $7.75bn. Future Fit savings, project-risk reduction and the proposed Built Environment sale were already underway.
already_announced_exclusion: The Future Fit programme and realised savings, $78m restructuring programme, Aegis Poland charge and remediation, Projects de-risking and move away from lump-sum work, proposed Built Environment sale, Russia exit and all related actions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Large revenue and earnings declines, statutory losses, severe cash outflow, rising debt and narrow covenant headroom support very high pressure. Better margin, a sharply larger order book and expected disposal proceeds provide meaningful but incomplete contrary evidence.

source_title: John Wood Group PLC Annual Report and Financial Statements 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 156, 170 and 246 state that the responsibility statement and Group and Company financial statements were approved by the Board on 28 March 2024; the exact Companies House filing bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Continuing revenue rose 7.9% to $5.90bn, adjusted EBITDA rose 8.9% to $422.7m and margin improved 10bps to 7.2%, with an order book of $6.27bn. Statutory continuing operations still lost $127.7m and free cash outflow remained $265m after interest, tax and $145m of exceptional cash flows. Net debt excluding leases increased to $693.5m from $393.2m and leverage rose to 2.08x, remaining below the 3.5x covenant. Adjusted operating cash flow improved to $194m and management expected further revenue and EBITDA growth. The prior Built Environment sale and simplification, portfolio and cost actions announced by approval were already in train.
already_announced_exclusion: The Built Environment disposal, portfolio disposals, contract-risk reduction, pricing and operational-delivery initiatives, restructuring and exceptional programmes, and the simplification and cost actions announced before report approval are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Growth, margin improvement and stronger operating cash coexist with a statutory loss, persistent free-cash outflow and materially higher debt. Covenant headroom, order growth and positive trading expectations provide strong but not decisive contrary evidence.
